messages.author: cf19475e9feb9344
messages.subject: Categorical variables
parts:
Hi all,

I'm new in lavaan and I'd like to ask a couple of questions:
  1. I've got categorical variables are exogenous (independent), and I have created dummy variables (0/1). Do I need to specify them in the cfa model as ordered? I did it anyway and I got warning messages that some of them are highly correlated. When I don't specify them in the model as ordered the model doesn't converge
  2. Can I fit a ML exploratory model in lavaan? 

Many thanks in advance

Vasilis

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables
parts:
Vasilis--
     Did you leave out 1 category from each categorical covariate--turning say a 4 category variable into 3 dummies?  And would you consider a different coding of the categories, which might produce less covariance?  Are responses unequally distributed across categories, such that covariances really should be high?
--Ed Rigdon

Sent from my iPad

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables
parts: Can I fit a ML exploratory model in lavaan?

If you are talking about exploratory factor analysis (EFA) in lavaan, look into the semTools package for functions

library(semTools)
?efaUnrotate


If you are talking about ESEM as implemented in Mplus, that is not available in lavaan

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables
parts:
On 05/19/2014 03:11 PM, vasilis nikolaou wrote:
>
> Hi all,
>
> I'm new in lavaan and I'd like to ask a couple of questions:
>
> 1. I've got categorical variables are exogenous (independent), and I

> have created dummy variables (0/1). Do I need to specify them in the
> cfa model as ordered? I did it anyway and I got warning messages
> that some of them are highly correlated. When I don't specify them
> in the model as ordered the model doesn't converge

You should not declare exogenous variables as 'ordered'. You need to
create dummy variables. If your categorical covariate has K levels, you
need K-1 dummy variables.

Yves.
